evidence: Single executable entry point (__main__.py, crypto_trading.py, backtest.py) with clear separation of concerns
Logical grouping into high-cohesion modules: models, strategies, API interfaces (binance_*_manager), utilities (logger, database, notifications, scheduler)
No inter-service communication or remote calls; all dependencies are internal Python imports
Shared domain models (Coin, Pair, Trade, etc.) used consistently across modules
Strategies inherit from a core class (AutoTrader), indicating vertical layering within a single deployment unit
Database and config are singletons/services shared across modules (e.g., AutoTrader, backtest, api_server)
API server uses in-process Flask + SocketIO, not a separate service, indicating single-binary architecture
risks: High fan-out (avg 4.96) and shared mutable state (e.g., Database, Config) may reduce testability and increase coupling over time
Lack of explicit ports/adapters boundaries could make future evolution toward microservices more costly
Strategy pattern is implemented via inheritance; could be more flexible via composition in larger systems
